$comment: Performance budgets (#108), checked by `npm run budgets` in CI's budgets job. Raise a number only in a pull request that says why. Kernel and viewport baselines are a CI runner's own medians (2 to 3 times a laptop's); the check fails when a median is over its baseline by more than the tolerance.

bundle.$comment: KB gzipped, per chunk. The shell is the JavaScript index.html loads before first paint. totalJs went from 600 to 620 in #312: main was already at 601.9 after the text tool (#309) added fonts (glyphs, 50 KB, loaded only when you place text), alongside the path tracer (63 KB, loaded only for Render); the shell cap is what guards first paint. The shell went from 355 to 358 in #310: main was at 354.6, and dragging an arm by its tool point (#176) adds 1.2 KB of glue (the tool marker, the palette commands, the lock toggle) after its solver and drag moved to a lazy chunk. 358 to 361 in the clash check (#178): main was at 357.9, and the check adds 0.8 KB (its state, the overlap boxes, the command); its list and the kernel work load later. What's new (#319) adds 0.4 KB (the Help entry, the command and the hook); the notes, the seen list, the card and the dialog load later. totalJs went from 620 to 630 with named poses (#177): main was at 618.1 and they add 1.9 KB; everything past first paint loads on use. The shell went from 355 to 356 when dragging into components (#334) added 1.1 KB (drop onto a row in the tree, the Move into menu, the moves saved with the model) to a main at 354.5. totalJs went from 630 to 632 with components (#171): main was at about 629.3 after the shell trim (#332) split code into lazy chunks, and components add 1.0 KB (the nested browser, the active component, two icons). The shell went from 361 to 362 for dropping a sketch point on another point or a line to join it (#326): main was at 360.7, and the drag glue adds 0.4 KB (the snap while dragging, the coincident on drop); finding what it drops on loads with the sketch. The clash sweep (#179) adds 0.1 KB (its command and the panel props); the sweep, its state and the mesh test load later. totalJs went from 632 to 636 for the Parameters dialog with Model parameters: main was at about 631.6, and the dialog's chunk grows by about 2.5 KB (the steps' sizes, the filter, the comment column); it loads only when Parameters opens, and the shell moves 0.3 KB. Revolve's axis pick (#342) took the shell from 357 to 358 and totalJs from 639 to 642: main was at the shell cap, and the step's axis state, the axis button and help add about 0.5 KB at first paint after the picking itself (axisPick) and Construct's pick geometry (pickGeo) moved to lazy chunks; the rest loads with the Revolve tool. #320 took the shell to under 355 and the cap back to 355: the move gizmo (TransformControls), the catalogue's parts list, file import and the problem report's zip code now load after first paint. totalJs went from 637 to 639 for the tips card (#340): main was at about 636.8, and the card and its tips add 1.3 KB in their own chunk, loaded only when it shows; the shell moves 0.3 KB (the hook, the Help entry, the bulb icon). Pattern of features (copy a hole or stub onto the same body, round a construction axis, #343) took the shell from 358 to 359 and totalJs from 642 to 644: main was at about 357.2 and 641.1, and it adds 0.8 KB to the shell (copying ops with moves in the kernel document, the axis pick, the step picked on the timeline, the release note) and about 0.8 KB more in the kernel worker (the same document code) and the lazy Pattern bar. Projecting faces as true circles and arcs (#349) took totalJs from 644 to 645: main was at 643.7, and it adds 0.5 KB (each face's B-rep edge list from the kernel worker, its use when projecting a face, hiding Fix marks on projected geometry, the release note); the shell moves 0.2 KB.

wasm.$comment: MB. OCCT is the opencascade.js build replicad ships (23 MB); the issue's 12 MB / 3.5 MB target needs a slimmer build of the same unmodified OCCT (#4, #50).

viewport.$comment: Since #204 the view fills the 1280 x 800 window (3.3 times the pixels it had), and the frame is 34 to 84 ms on runners depending on the runner (the kernel numbers swing by the same factor in the same runs). Baseline 90 leaves the same headroom over a fast runner as the kernel budgets have.

lighthouse.$comment: Desktop preset, Chromium with SwiftShader as CI runs it. Software WebGL compiles the view's shaders on the main thread (about 1 s of blocking time); with WebGL off the score is 100. The target is 0.85.
